old_title: Cheltenham November meeting horse racing - live
new_title: Meetmebythesea wins Paddy Power Gold Cup as Paul Nicholls matches Martin Pipe wins record - as it happened
old_text:
A steady early pace as you'd expect at three miles.
Thank You Ma'am is prominent, he generally makes the running. Reallyntruthfully is also close to the lead, Doctor On Call travelling well in fourth.
The favourite is going well, but Kildinan Prince is sat last, albeit travelling well enough.
A circuit to go, Doctor On Call's backers will be pleased to see him still going well in fourth. Kildinan Prince, though, has all but one of the field in front of him.
There are fewer issues with non-runners over at Windsor, where the ground is good, good-to-soft in places, and 12 runners go to post for the first of two races from the riverside track on the ITV Racing schedule.
Doctor On Call, a summer switcher from Paul Nicholls's yard to Sam Thomas, is the narrow market leader at 5-2 to follow up a four-and-a-quarter length success in a three-runner race at Ludlow back in February. It's limited form and he has been off the track for 269 days, but Thomas is a dab hand at getting them ready first time up.
Emma Lavelle's Kildinian Prince is his main market rival, making his handicap debut off a very workable mark of 120 having shed his maiden tag in a three-runner race at Exeter in March.
Heading away from the stands now, Atomic City has passed Tiny Riot but is still second-last.
Down the back, Magnetude has taken over in front, all bar Tiny Riot covered by three lengths behind.
Three to jump, still Magnetude in front, Charles Darnay and Atomic City both going well.
Now Charles Darnay jumps into second at the third-last. Atomic City making eye-catching progress on the bridle too.
Over the second-last, Charles Darnay has a narrow lead turning in but Atomic City goes well too.
They're in the air together but Atomic City is going best, he's quicker away from the final hurdle too and going clear, putting down a big marker for the Triumph Hurdle back here in March!
More money for Atomic City just before the off, he's down to 6-5 with Charles Darnay out to 3-1. Admiral Will Brown is a 4-1 shot and James Owen's second-string, Magnetude, has also been nibbled at, down to 17-2.
Just under 10 minutes to the off in the Triumph Hurdle Trial and there is still plenty of money for Atomic City, currently trading at around 11-8. Charles Darnay is attracting backers too, though, at 9-4, while Admiral Will Brown, who was rated 78 on the Flat and won his hurdles debut at Down Royal in October, is also lively in the market at 9-2.
There was fine display of jumping for the big Saturday crowd to enjoy in the opener, as Oran McGill got into an excellent rhythm on Dinoland and comfortably held Little Ledgend by six lengths.
JonPullin, Cheltenham's clerk of the course, has been discussing the ground and slew of non-runners on Racing TV.
"We're comfortable that we did everything we could and got as much water on as possible ahead of the meeting," Pullin said.
"When we finished irrigating on Thursday afternoon ahead of Thursday night's frost we were comfortable there was enough moisture in the ground. We were hopeful that would hold for yesterday and today because we knew realistically we couldn't get anymore water on due to the frost.
"As it transpired we had a sharper frost than forecast and that sharpened it up on Thursday into Friday and the same last night so we've gone good, good to firm in places but the majority is good.
"With irrigation and the little rain we have had between the Showcase [meeting in October] and this one, we have put 400mm on, but we've only had 16mm of rain."
With the two star names in the Arkle Trial at 1.45 both scratched, this is now the main supporting act on Saturday's card in some respects, as there are a couple of very interesting juvenile prospects in opposition.
Charles Darnay, whose trainer, James Owen, is hoping to win this race for the third time in four years, was the early favourite after the declarations on Thursday, but has since been supplanted by Joseph O'Brien's Atomic City, who was a lightly-raced maiden winner on the Flat but looked a natural over hurdles when making a successful debut at Cork last month (in this video at 1m10sec).
Charles Darnay, meanwhile, was also highly impressive on his hurdling debut, at Wetherby.
There is very little to pick between the pair of them on that (limited) evidence, but personally I plumped for Atomic City, mainly because his maiden event at Cork was run in an excellent time for the grade and he won with plenty to spare.
They are on the way to post at Cheltenham for the opener, a handicap chase for amateur riders over three miles and a furlong, and the going is now good, good-to-firm in places.
Transmission, Top Guy and Jaccours are all non-runners here, leaving nine runners and a market headed by Olly Murphy's Little Ledgend at 11-4.
Hello and welcome to the Guardian's live-blog coverage of what should be one of the great days in the jumping calendar: Paddy Power Gold Cup day at Cheltenham's November meeting.
Unfortunately, though, "should be" is doing the kind of heavy lifting in that sentence that Red Rum achieved in his second Grand National victory in 1974, because the prevailing fast ground has already seen the card shorn of several star names, and around two dozen of the original declarations in all.
The original field of 15 for the Paddy Power Gold Cup, perhaps the biggest handicap chase in the first half of the winter campaign, is now down to 10 runners - July Flower is the latest absentee - while the "Big Two" in the Grade Two Arkle Trial - Kabral Du Mathan and Old Park Star, last year's Supreme Novice Hurdle winner, are scratches too.
It is disappointing and also deeply frustrating for the track, as it is difficult to know what else Jon Pullin, the clerk of the course, could have done. Sub-zero temperatures overnight meant that he was unable to switch on the taps on Thursday or Friday, and there has been so little rain for months, rather than just weeks, that even watered ground is unlikely to be any easier than good.
The 30k racegoers expected through the gates still have a busy afternoon to look forward to, though, kicking off with a handicap chase for amateur riders at 12.35 before the ITV Racing action begins with the Grade Two Triumph Hurdle Trial at 1.10. There are a couple of top-class prospects in that race - Atomic City, backed down to favourite this morning, and Charles Darnay - while the Paddy Power Gold Cup is due to be off and running at 2.20.
new_text:
MEETMEBYTHESEA ENDS MCMANUS'S WAIT FOR PADDY POWER GOLD CUP WINNER
JP McManus, one of jump racing's leading owners for four decades, finally got his hands on the trophy for the Paddy Power Gold Cup on Saturday as Meetmebythesea, the 2-1 favourite, held the challenge of BluekingD'Oroux (100-30) by two-and-a-half lengths in the feature event of Cheltenham's November meeting.
The race was one of several on the card that suffered a series of non-runners due to drying ground, which was officially good, good-to-firm by the start of the first race, but Harry Cobden's mount delivered the result that many in the crowd of more than 32k racegoers wanted to see and gave the jockey his first big-race success since signing a retainer to ride as McManus's No.1.
"This is the race that really made me tick growing up," Ben Pauling, Meetmebytheseas's trainer, said, "and I've been coming to this meeting since I was 14. This has always been a big race for me and to have the favourite was a dream, so to win it is even better.
"I had so much faith in this horse and I talked him up plenty in the lead up. It's all well sitting on the fence, but I knew he was good, just not how good. You just have to believe he is going to keep on improving and hopefully that puts him bang there for some of the better races."
Meetmebythesea could now step up into Grade One company as soon as the King George VI Chase at Kempton on Boxing Day, for which he is quoted at around 12-1 by bookmakers.
Pauling won the race last year with The Jukebox Man and sees Meetmebythesea as having similar quality.
"I suppose we have to think about Kempton at Christmas and I think he's going to stay every yard of three miles," Pauling said. "To keep a horse like this improving is cool and we need these types of horses to keep us going the right way. It's not easy when you're in the top 10 and you need to find horses of this calibre. He looks to be one of them."
At Windsor, Fasol's victory in a handicap hurdle moved Paul Nicholls, his trainer, alongside Martin Pipe's all-time record of 3,930 British jumps winners. He has a single runner on Sunday's Cheltenham card - Pourquoi Pas Papa in the 1.25 - as he attempts to take sole control of the record.
More than half of the original field of 13 declared runners are out of the final race on the ITV card, including Nicholls's A King Of Magic, who would have gone to post with a leading chance.
Daylatedollarshort is the market leader now for Olly Murphy's yard. He is back up in trip by a furlong-and-a-half after winning a big-field event at Chepstow last time, while Hillberry Hill, trained by Kim Bailey & Mat Nicholls, is next in in the betting. He's the most lightly-raced runner in the field, with just three starts to his name, and was an impressive winner of a novice event at Southwell in March. This is his handicap debut and an opening mark of 122 could be lenient.
Kapitein Kool takes them along early, with Anniversary in close attendance.
Secret Squirrel is fifth, Zarakerjack poised in fourth going well.
Watamu also travelling nicely, but Kapitein Kool still leads and going well.
Three out, turning in, Watamu is going really well and moves forward.
Over the last, Watamu and Fasol are together, they're fighting for the line, this is going to be very close .... PHOTO! And this could be Paul Nicholls's record-equalling winner if Fasol gets the verdict.
It's off to Windsor now on ITV for the 3.10, a two-mile handicap hurdle with Zarakerjack favourite at 11-4 and Watamu and Secret Squirrel - a past winner over track and trip - next in on 4-1.
A perfectly-judged front-running ride by Michael Keneally. He had an easy time of it on the lead at a track where it generally pays to be handy in any case, but was a half-length down over the last before summoning enough from his mount to reclaim the lead.
Black Bamboo has had an easy time of it on the lead here, still has a handy lead turning down the hill. But he dives at the third-last! Lost momentum but still on his feet and going ok.
William Yeats making ominous progress now, he's moving up alongside Black Bamboo as they turn in.
Up to the last, Black Bamboo just leads, can he hold on? Yes! What a brave performance from the front, William Yeats looked to have his measure but BlackBamboo found more.
Off and running in the 2.55 at Cheltenham - BUT THE GAMBLE WAS RELUCTANT TO STRIDE! Margaret's Legacy finally gets going but trails the second-last runner by 10 lengths early.
The springer in the market for the next race here is Warren Greatrex's Margaret'sLegacy, who has been backed from 16-1 to 13-2. That's a fair old plunge.
The crowdfigure for today's card is in. They were hoping for around 30k, and in fact, they got more than 32k: a total of 32,618 to be precise. That's the best for this card since the post-Covid bounce-back year of 2021, and the favourite's win in the big race is likely to be the main memory they take home, rather than the unusually thin fields.
Another of the races on today's card that has suffered from a series of non-runners, with six of the original 16 declarations now sitting it out.
That leaves Sam England's William Yeats as the narrow 5-2 favourite from Ifiwerearichman and Aimeric on 7-2. Rambo T is a 9-2 shot and it is 12-1 bar the four.
JP McManus is chatting to ITV Racing after his first Paddy Power Gold Cup success.
At the last, the other horse was going very well but I did think ours might find a bit. [Harry Cobden] is at the top of his game and I think he's as good as there is. I'm very lucky to have him.
Harry Cobden spoke to ITV Racing's Alice Plunkett after his Paddy Power Gold Cup win on Meetmebythesea.
These big days don't come along all that often and I'm going to enjoy every one of them from now on. You just have to pinch yourself when you're in this position.
Harry Cobden is absolutely buzzing after that win, his first big-race success in the famous green-and-gold colours of JP McManus. He punched the air passing the post and is beaming from ear-to-ear on the way back to unsaddle.
Down to the last, Blueking D'Oroux leads from Meetmebythesea, will he get a good jump?
No! He's slow at the last and surrenders the advantage, Meetmebythesea was quicker and leads on the hill, he's staying on well and Blueking D'Oroux won't get there, it's a first Paddy Power Gold Cup for JP McManus!
